newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Wallonia offers to meet Clabecq losses.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Wallonia offers to meet Clabecq losses.

text.p: Belgium's Walloon Regional Government said on Friday it was prepared to meet operating losses at Forges de Clabecq after the bankrupt steel maker was placed in receivership by a commercial court.

"Wallonia President (Robert Collignon) has informed the court that he is ready and willing to guarantee, through (steel investment company) SWS...the receivers against all operating losses arising from the continuation of activities," the region said in a statement.
The Walloon Region, through SWS, was Clabecq's majority shareholder and biggest creditor.

A Belgian commercial court declared the troubled steel maker bankrupt on Friday but appointed four receivers to run the company, whose order book is full for at least three months, for an unspecified time.

Clabecq's 1,800 workers would be given their notice, but as many as 1,350 would be immediately re-employed, Belgian radio reported. Unions said they would meet on Saturday to consider their response to the court's decision.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy in mid-December after the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc ($47 million) rescue plan by the Walloon Region, which then withdrew its support for the firm.
The Commission's decision has been challenged by both Clabecq's unions and the regional government.
